facts.text: I am looking to create a project roadmap for a new project I am about to start.
I attended a project management workshop last weekend on Saturday and Sunday.
The project management workshop was held at the downtown convention center.
I learned about agile methodologies at the workshop.
I am planning to start a project to develop a mobile app for tracking personal expenses.
The project duration is expected to be around 6 months.
I will be working with a team of 5 people including myself.
My team and I are familiar with agile methodologies.
My team and I are open to using Scrum or Kanban.
The project scope is well-defined.
There is uncertainty involved because we are not sure about some technical details.
I am thinking of breaking the project into smaller tasks and estimating the effort required for each task.
I have never done this before.
I want tips on how to estimate the effort required for each task correctly.
I think I will try the three-point estimation technique.
I want an example of applying three-point estimation to a user story about registering for the app using email address and password.
I think I will apply the three-point estimation technique to the other user stories as well.
I attended the project management workshop last weekend and the speaker Rachel mentioned something about effort estimation in agile projects.
I wish I had taken more notes on effort estimation.
I am planning to review my notes from the project management workshop.
I want to find information on effort estimation in agile projects in my workshop notes.
I think Rachel may have mentioned specific techniques or best practices that I can apply to my project.
